summary.tldr: Creates a federal law to designate places, persons and events of national significance, protect heritage sites and archaeological resources, and repeal the current sites and monuments law.
what_it_does: Creates a system to designate places, persons and events of national significance or national interest.
Sets the federal minister’s duties for designations, protection of heritage value, protection of archaeological resources, and work on the World Heritage Convention.
Continues the federal board that advises on sites and monuments, and adds representatives for First Nations, Inuit and Métis.
Requires a public register of designated places, persons and events, and lets some information be kept out in some cases.
Requires federal ministers and certain Crown corporations to consider conservation standards and consult Parks Canada before physical changes or disposal of some designated places.
Creates a program to commemorate deceased prime ministers at their grave sites or other appropriate places.
